# Code review: PR 8458 (1.5.0 trust lists)

**Scope:** `c9b7d88…HEAD`, committed work only. 9 files, +150 −6, base `1bfc0a8` (merge-base) → `6c592b0`.

Read-only run: I didn't run tests, install dependencies, use `gh`, or write `.git/safe-code-review/last-run.tsv`, so there's no "since your last run" section.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Ready to open |
| **Score** | 97 / 100 (1 of 2 findings adjudicated) |
| **Held it down** | The same Safe version lists are copied in several places, so each one had to be edited by hand |
| **Fix first** | Nothing blocks. Two P3 tidy-ups, both optional |

The change adds `'1.5.0'` to six allow-lists of official Safe contracts: the Security Hub's known-version list, fallback-handler list and factory check, the untrusted-fallback-handler hook, and the MultiSend and SignMessageLib guards. I checked the installed `safe-deployments` package and `types-kit` 4.0.1. Every address the tests use is a real canonical mainnet 1.5.0 deployment, and each differs from its 1.4.1 counterpart. So if the change were reverted, every new test would fail.

## Scores by area

| Area | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| DRY | 88 | 2 × P3 |
| Security | 100 | Only official addresses from `safe-deployments` were added. No new trust in anything user-supplied |
| Bugs | 100 | `hasMatchingDeployment` checks each version independently (`.some`), so adding one version can't change results for the others |
| Regression | 100 | Lists only get longer. Nothing was removed or renamed |
| Testing | 100 | Each widened list has a test for the new version. `isMigrateToL2TxData` also gains a rejection test for an unknown MultiSend |
| Architecture | 100 | No new modules or imports |
| KISS | 100 | |
| Conventions | 100 | Test comments and `!` non-null assertions follow the existing tests |
| Performance | n/a | Constant-size lists |

## Worth a ticket

**F1 · P3 · DRY · CONFIRMED (a second agent tried to refute it and couldn't)**
`apps/web/src/features/security/data/scanners/constants.ts:12`
- **What:** `KNOWN_SAFE_VERSIONS` is a second copy of the exported `SAFE_VERSIONS` (`packages/utils/src/services/contracts/utils.ts:6`). Same six versions, just in reverse order, and that one already includes `1.5.0`.
- **Why it matters:** Order doesn't matter to `hasMatchingDeployment`, and apps/web already imports `SAFE_VERSIONS` (`safe-migrations.ts:15`, `safeUpdateParams.ts:19`). Using it would have made this edit unnecessary, and the two lists can drift apart when the next version ships.
- **Fix:** Delete `KNOWN_SAFE_VERSIONS`. Import `SAFE_VERSIONS` in `contractVersion.ts:13-14` and `factoryValidation.ts:7`.

**F2 · P3 · DRY · not adjudicated (counts at full weight)**
The same inline list `['1.3.0', '1.4.1', '1.5.0']` now appears in 3 files, and the PR edited each copy separately:
- `apps/web/src/utils/transaction-guards.ts:160`
- `apps/web/src/utils/transaction-guards.ts:420`
- `apps/web/src/hooks/useHasUntrustedFallbackHandler.ts:29-33`
- `apps/web/src/features/security/data/scanners/fallbackHandler.ts:17`

The next version bump will need the same four edits, and missing one would silently mark an official contract as untrusted. The repo already derives this set in one place: `packages/utils/src/services/contracts/bytecodeComparison.ts:13` uses `SAFE_VERSIONS.filter((v) => !isLegacyVersion(v))`. **Fix:** export one "1.3.0 and later" constant built that way and use it at all four sites.

## Your call

| # | Finding | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Duplicate of `SAFE_VERSIONS` | Fix now (about 3 lines) or ticket |
| F2 | 4 inline copies of the "1.3.0 and later" list | Ticket, ideally together with F1 |

## Worth tidying (optional, no effect on the score)

1. `apps/web/src/features/security/data/scanners/fallbackHandler.ts:19`: the JSDoc says 1.5.0 is "not in SafeVersion type yet". That's false, because `types-kit` 4.0.1's `SafeVersion` includes `'1.5.0'`, and line 17 now puts `'1.5.0'` in a `SafeVersion[]`. **Fix:** drop the parenthetical. It's one line.

This started as a finding, but a second agent ruled it out as a finding against this PR: the comment was already wrong at the base commit, so this diff didn't introduce it.

## Not sure about these

- `packages/utils/src/features/multichain/hooks/useCompatibleNetworks.ts:15`: `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` is still `['1.4.1', '1.3.0']`. That means a 1.5.0 Safe probably can't be added to another network. This is multichain replication rather than "trust", so leaving it out may be deliberate, but the commit title says "across the app". Please confirm the scope.

## Not checked

- **Tests weren't run,** because you asked me not to. I read the test logic and checked the addresses by hand.
- **Package version mismatch:** I checked addresses against `safe-deployments` 1.37.63 from the main checkout. This branch's lockfile pins 1.37.61, and I didn't confirm the 1.5.0 files are the same in that version.
- **The migration view with the 1.5.0 MultiSend:** I didn't check how `MigrationToL2TxData` (reached from `TxData/index.tsx:128`) shows the other steps of a migration batch. The 1.5.0 MultiSend reads a zero `to` address as the Safe itself (`packages/utils/src/utils/multiSend.ts:10`), which the 1.4.1 one doesn't. I'm not aware of any flaw here; I just didn't look.

## How this was produced

I read all nine changed files and the code around them myself, checked versions and addresses in the installed packages, and searched every caller of `hasMatchingDeployment` and every `SafeVersion[]` list. For adjudication I ran one refuter agent per finding. F1 held up; the stale comment was ruled out as a finding against this PR and moved to tidying. F2 wasn't adjudicated, so it keeps full weight in the score.
